mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% signals a strengthening demand in the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economic activity improves.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals an improving labor market, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges and reduced output.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals inflationary pressure combined with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 4%
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points, signals robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month and UNRATE decrease > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over three months signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth rate falls below 2% annually and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a supply-side slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth < 2% and INDPRO decrease > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.
